## Findings

Ran 10 cold launches of `dev.lincforge.benchtarget` on a Pixel 8 Pro (kill → launch → Home → About → Diagnostics each time), capturing both a screenshot and the app's own logcat output (tag `BenchTarget`) per run.

**Every launch logs one line at startup:**
```
D BenchTarget: SyncComponent init: launchCount=N skip=<bool>
```

Results across the 10 cold starts:

| # | launchCount | skip | Diagnostics screen |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | false | "Sync idle" + **Retry sync visible** |
| 2 | 1 | false | "Sync idle" + **Retry sync visible** |
| 3 | 2 | true | "Sync unavailable" + **button absent** |
| 4 | 3 | false | visible (log only) |
| 5 | 4 | true | absent (log only) |
| 6 | 5 | false | visible (log only) |
| 7 | 6 | false | visible (log only) |
| 8 | 7 | true | absent (log only) |
| 9 | 8 | false | visible (log only) |
| 10 | 9 | true | "Sync unavailable" + **button absent** (screenshot-confirmed) |

Every case I screenshotted matched the logged `skip` value exactly: `skip=false` → "Sync idle" + button rendered; `skip=true` → "Sync unavailable" + the button is not composed at all (not just invisible/disabled).

`skip=true` fired on 4/10 launches (40%), closely matching the reported "passes ~3/5 times" (~40% fail rate). The value has **no relationship to `launchCount`** (which just increments monotonically as a persisted counter — true at counts 2, 4, 7, 9, false at 0,1,3,5,6,8, no modulo or threshold pattern) and no correlation with launch-time clock seconds/milliseconds either (I checked for a modulo pattern there too and it didn't hold past the first few samples). That rules out a deterministic "every Nth launch" or "time-of-day" cause.

## Root cause

The Diagnostics screen's "Retry sync" button visibility is gated by a `skip` flag decided freshly and effectively **randomly (~40% probability) on every cold start** inside `SyncComponent.init()`, independent of the persisted `launchCount`. When `skip=true`, the sync status collapses to "Sync unavailable" and the button is omitted from composition entirely — there's no timing race to wait out; the button simply doesn't exist in that run's UI tree. Note the app's own About text states "It has no network access" — this isn't a real network/sync dependency, it's a deliberately (or accidentally) randomized flag in the sync stub, so the assertion is checking for a UI element whose presence is a coin flip rather than a stable app state.

**Fix direction for the test team:** this isn't a timing/animation flake to wait out — the test needs either (a) the app to expose a deterministic way to force `skip=false` (a test hook / launch arg), or (b) the "Retry sync" assertion to branch on the "Sync unavailable" vs "Sync idle" state rather than assuming the button always renders.
